scope: src/main.js lines 30740-32600 (skins, screen shake, enemy hp adjust, building map canvas, radial menu, zone names, attachment tier, menu3d, story objective rig, objective init, tutorial, intro, level select) + verification of callers/definitions elsewhere in main.js

findings.title: Combo milestone FX fire twice per milestone (double toast, double money, double slowmo)
findings.description: The comboKill wrapper calls _comboMilestoneFx on every (count%5===0 && count<=30). But the underlying comboKill (the function declaration at 35985) ALREADY calls _comboMilestoneFx on every count%5===0 (line 36005). So _comboMilestoneFx runs twice for combo counts 5/10/15/20/30: two STREAK/MASSACRE/etc banners overlap, P.money+=count*20 is added twice (line 32440), moneyPopup shows twice, the ascending fanfare SFX plays twice (phasing/doubled volume), the kill-beat flash double-triggers, and triggerKillCamSlowMo(.55,.50) fires twice at count>=10.
findings.evidence: wrapper 32459-32461: `_origComboKill(isHead); if(P.combo&&P.combo.count%5===0&&P.combo.count<=30){ _comboMilestoneFx(P.combo.count); }` while the original comboKill at 36005 already does `if(P.combo.count%5===0&&typeof _comboMilestoneFx==='function')_comboMilestoneFx(P.combo.count);`
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate milestone call inside the wrapper at lines 32460-32462 (the original comboKill already fires it). Keep the wrapper only if it adds something else; here it adds nothing else, so the whole wrapper at 32457-32463 can be deleted. Safest surgical change: delete lines 32460-32462 (the `if(...){_comboMilestoneFx(...)}` block) so the wrapper just forwards.
findings.risk: Very low. After removing the duplicate, milestones fire exactly once (the design intent). No save-compat impact. Note: also fixes the related arg-drop bug below if you delete the whole wrapper.

findings.title: comboKill wrapper drops the opts arg (source/closeRange), starving the story-combat feel system
findings.description: Every kill site calls comboKill(isHead, {source, closeRange}) (e.g. lines 14490, 20165, 21433, 25239, 26451, 26557, 27664). The wrapper at 32458 is `function(isHead){ _origComboKill(isHead); ... }` — it never forwards the second argument. The real comboKill (36004) feeds opts.source and opts.closeRange into applyStoryCombatReward; with the wrapper in place those are always undefined, so applyStoryCombatReward receives source:'combo-kill' and closeRange:0 for EVERY kill regardless of weapon/range. This silently neuters the per-kill momentum/feel differentiation that the recent feel work added.
findings.evidence: 32458 `comboKill=function(isHead){` and 32459 `_origComboKill(isHead);` (no opts), versus the definition 35985 `function comboKill(isHead,opts={})` and 36004 `applyStoryCombatReward(P,{source:(opts&&opts.source)||'combo-kill',killed:true,isHead,combo:P.combo.count,closeRange:(opts&&opts.closeRange)||0});`
findings.fix: Delete the entire wrapper (32457-32463) — it is redundant once the double-milestone is removed and the original already handles milestones. If the wrapper must stay for some reason, change it to `comboKill=function(isHead,opts){ _origComboKill(isHead,opts); }` so opts is forwarded.
findings.risk: Very low. Deleting the wrapper restores the original two-arg behavior. Confirm no other override of comboKill exists (only this one found).

findings.title: autoFocus perk focus regen applied multiple times (tickFocus wrapper duplicates work the original already does)
findings.description: applyPerks2 sets P._focusRegen=1.35 when autoFocus is owned. The tickFocus wrapper (31091) adds an EXTRA regen of dt*.18*(P._focusRegen-1) when P._focusRegen>1, then calls _origTickFocus. But the original tickFocus (26982-26983) already multiplies regen by regenMul=(P._focusRegen||1)*(hasPerk('autoFocus')?1.25:1.0). So with autoFocus the focus bar regenerates from three stacked sources: the wrapper's extra term, the _focusRegen multiplier inside the original, and the additional 1.25 hasPerk multiplier inside the original. Focus fills far faster than the perk description implies.
findings.fix: Delete the extra regen block in the wrapper (31092-31095) so only the original applies the multiplier; the wrapper then just forwards. Better: drop the wrapper at 31090-31097 entirely and rely on the original's regenMul (which already reads P._focusRegen and hasPerk('autoFocus')). Also reconcile the redundant double-count: the original multiplies by BOTH P._focusRegen (1.35) AND hasPerk('autoFocus') 1.25 — pick one source of truth.
findings.risk: Low. Removing the wrapper slows autoFocus regen to the intended single-multiplier rate; only affects players who own the autoFocus perk.

findings.title: Radial quick-select menu is non-functional — never exits pointer lock, mouse can't hover/click slots
findings.description: openRadial builds DOM slots that rely on mouseenter (hover highlight) and mousedown (select+switchWeapon). But unlike showFullMap (31259) and showLoadoutViewer (32508), openRadial never calls document.exitPointerLock(). During gameplay pointer lock is active (locked=true), so the cursor is captured/hidden and cannot hover or click the slots. There is also no keyboard-number fallback while RADIAL.open. Net result: the player can open the radial (CapsLock) but can never select a weapon from it, then it closes on key release. The tutorial even advertises this feature ('Hold CAPS for radial weapon select', line 30817).
findings.evidence: openRadial 31407 `const r=$e('radial');if(!r)return;` ... 31425 `slot.addEventListener('mousedown',()=>{ switchWeapon(i);closeRadial(); });` with no exitPointerLock; compare showFullMap 31259 `if(locked)try{document.exitPointerLock();}catch(_){}`
findings.fix: In openRadial after RADIAL.open=true add `if(locked)try{document.exitPointerLock();}catch(_){}` and in closeRadial re-lock with `if(RADIAL.open===false&&G.started&&!P.dead&&!G.menuOpen)tryLock();` (or restore lock in the keyup handler). Alternatively (lower risk, keeps pointer lock) add a keydown handler that maps Digit1..DigitN to slots while RADIAL.open and select on key.
findings.risk: Low-medium. Exiting pointer lock mid-combat momentarily frees the cursor; re-lock on close. The hold-to-open / release-to-close UX with CapsLock (a toggle key whose keyup timing is OS-dependent) may need testing, but the core fix (exit lock so slots are clickable) is what makes the feature work at all.

findings.title: OBJECTIVE_DEFS stealth/timer objectives fail the wrong building mastery (B07/B10 mismatch)
findings.description: OBJECTIVE_DEFS (31868) declares B07='quiet the deck' stealth and B10='reach the bell tower' timer, and tickObjective sets G.mastery.failed=true on alarm (32166) / on timeout (32203). But the campaign's actual mastery for B07 is 'yacht_no_heal' (No-Heal Boarding, CAMPAIGN_LEVELS line 37266) and for B10 is 'cathedral_silent_choir' (don't fire in the nave, line 37273). So being seen on the yacht fails the player's No-Heal mastery even though no heal was used, and the bell-tower timer expiring fails the Silent-Choir mastery even though the player never fired in the nave. Two parallel objective systems write to the same G.mastery.failed flag with unrelated conditions.
findings.evidence: OBJECTIVE_DEFS 31871 `7: {kind:'stealth',...}` 31873 `10:{kind:'timer',timerS:90,...}`; tickObjective 32166 `if(G.mastery)G.mastery.failed=true;` (stealth alarm) and 32203 `if(G.mastery)G.mastery.failed=true;` (timer expiry). Campaign mastery for B07 is yacht_no_heal (37266) and B10 is cathedral_silent_choir (37273).
findings.fix: Either (a) gate the G.mastery.failed writes in tickObjective behind a check that the active building's mastery.id matches this objective's intent, or (b) decouple objective failure from mastery entirely (these objectives already have their own o.failed/announce flow at 32239) and let only the genuine mastery conditions (heal use at 37163, firing-in-nave detection) toggle G.mastery.failed. Remove lines 32166 and 32203's `if(G.mastery)G.mastery.failed=true;` for buildings whose mastery is unrelated.
findings.risk: Low. Mastery is meta-progress (PROGRESS.mastery); current behavior wrongly denies it. No save shape change.

findings.title: Enemy HP never scales with difficulty — _adjustEnemyHp / DIFF_HP_MUL / DIFFICULTY_MODIFIERS are all dead, descriptions promise tougher enemies
findings.description: _adjustEnemyHp(e) (30975) multiplies enemy maxHp/hp by DIFF_HP_MUL but is never called anywhere (grep finds zero callers). DIFFICULTY_MODIFIERS.enemyHp (30867/30873/30879) and DIFF_HP_MUL (30974) are never read by gameplay. The only real difficulty scaling is player-damage-taken (_difficultyDamageScale 37123) and score multipliers (35202/36996/38463). So on Hard/Lethal the enemies hit the player harder but have IDENTICAL health to Normal, directly contradicting DIFFICULTY_MODIFIERS descriptions ('Tougher AI', enemyHp 1.30/1.65) and DIFF_DESCRIPTIONS. The Veteran/Expert promise of tougher enemies is unfulfilled.
findings.evidence: 30975-30980 `function _adjustEnemyHp(e){ ...const mul=DIFF_HP_MUL[G.difficulty||'normal']||1.0; e.maxHp=Math.round(e.maxHp*mul); e.hp=e.maxHp; }` with no caller; 30867 `enemyHp:1.0,...` / 30873 `enemyHp:1.30,...` / 30879 `enemyHp:1.65,...` never referenced.
findings.fix: Call _adjustEnemyHp(e) from the Enemy spawn/init path (e.g. right after each `new Enemy(...)` in waves, or inside the Enemy constructor after hp/maxHp are set, gated by G.difficulty!=='normal'). Pick ONE multiplier table as source of truth (DIFF_HP_MUL) and delete the duplicates (DIFFICULTY_MODIFIERS.enemyHp, DIFF_DESCRIPTIONS) or wire them in. Take care boss hp is handled separately (don't double-scale lieutenants which already *=1.5 at 32982).
findings.risk: Medium — changes combat balance on Hard/Lethal and could affect leaderboards/mastery times. Apply behind difficulty!=='normal' and verify boss/lieutenant aren't double-scaled.

findings.title: Four competing difficulty tables with disagreeing values
findings.description: DIFFICULTY_MODIFIERS (30864) says lethal enemyDamage:1.85; DIFF_DESCRIPTIONS (31669) says lethal mul:2.0; DIFF_HP_MUL (30974) lethal 1.65; the live damage scale _difficultyDamageScale (37124) uses 1.85; the live score scales use 1.45 (35202), 2.0 (36996), 1.85 (38463). The three tables in this scope (DIFFICULTY_MODIFIERS, DIFF_HP_MUL, DIFF_DESCRIPTIONS) are never read by gameplay and disagree with each other and with the live inline literals. Pure dead/contradictory metadata that will mislead future edits and any UI that reads DIFF_DESCRIPTIONS.
findings.fix: Collapse to a single difficulty config object that the live code (_difficultyDamageScale, enemy hp scaling, score) reads from, and delete the unused DIFFICULTY_MODIFIERS/DIFF_DESCRIPTIONS/DIFF_HP_MUL duplicates. If a difficulty-select UI needs descriptions, point it at the single source.
findings.risk: Low if you only delete the unread tables. If you unify and re-point live code, re-balance and re-verify probes.

findings.title: Scripted cinematic building-intro flythrough is fully implemented but never triggered
findings.description: startBuildingIntro (31818) sets up a 4-phase camera flythrough, a cinematic whoosh SFX, and a building-name overlay; tickIntro (32293) runs it every frame gated on INTRO.active. But startBuildingIntro is never called anywhere (only INTRO.active=true is inside startBuildingIntro itself). So the intro never fires — the loop ticks tickIntro every frame for nothing, and a polished, AAA-feeling level-reveal is dark. References BUILDING_INFO[G.building-1].name which exists.
findings.evidence: grep: only occurrences of startBuildingIntro are its definition (31818) and INTRO.active=true (31820) inside it; no caller. tickIntro is called at 41613 but immediately returns since INTRO.active is false.
findings.fix: Call startBuildingIntro() at building start — e.g. inside startBuilding after the level is built and camera positioned (near 35396/35405) and guard with a setting/first-time flag so it can be skipped. Ensure G._introLockedInput is honored by the input/movement code (it sets the flag but verify movement actually reads it). Low-risk visible payoff for the moment you enter a level.
findings.risk: Medium — must verify G._introLockedInput actually suppresses player movement/look during the 4.5s, and that camera control is cleanly handed back (tickIntro restores at 32307-32312). Test that it doesn't fight the existing spawn camera.

findings.title: _initMenu3D (main-menu world-behind props) never called; if wired would leak boxes
findings.description: _initMenu3D adds 8 faux building boxes to the scene for a 'world behind the menu' look and pushes them into MENU3D.particles, but the function is never called. Besides being dead, there is no teardown: MENU3D.particles meshes/geometry are never removed/disposed when the game starts, so if it were ever wired in it would leak geometry + leave menu props in the gameplay scene.
findings.evidence: 31797 `function _initMenu3D(){` with no caller; 31811 `b.position.set(...);scn.add(b);MENU3D.particles.push(b);` and no disposal/removal path for MENU3D.particles anywhere.
findings.fix: Either delete _initMenu3D + MENU3D (dead) or, if used for menu polish, add a teardown that scene.remove()s and geometry.dispose()s every MENU3D.particles entry when G.started becomes true, and call _initMenu3D only on the menu screen.
findings.risk: Low. Currently inert. Only relevant if someone wires it; flag prevents a future leak.

findings.title: TUTORIAL_SEQ / TUTOR / tickTutorialHints is a third, dead tutorial system overlapping ONBOARD
findings.description: There are three onboarding systems: ONBOARD/tickOnboard (gated on PROGRESS.seenTutorialOnboard, actually ticked at 41612), the interactive TUTORIAL_STEPS/tickTutorial (gated on PROGRESS._tutorialSeen, ticked at 41614), and TUTORIAL_SEQ/TUTOR/tickTutorialHints (30807-30851). tickTutorialHints is never called and also reads PROGRESS.seenTutorialOnboard (the ONBOARD flag) — so even if called it would be suppressed once ONBOARD completes. It writes to the same #onboard-card element ONBOARD uses, which would conflict if both ran. It is pure dead, redundant code that can mislead future edits about which tutorial is authoritative.
findings.evidence: 30828 `function tickTutorialHints(){ if(!TUTOR.active||PROGRESS.seenTutorialOnboard)return; ...}` no caller; targets `$e('onboard-card')` (30843) which is also driven by tickOnboard (32611).
findings.fix: Delete TUTORIAL_SEQ, TUTOR, and tickTutorialHints (30807-30851). Keep ONBOARD (the live one) and the interactive TUTORIAL_STEPS path. Confirms no caller before deleting.
findings.risk: Low. Removing dead code; verify no probe references TUTORIAL_SEQ/TUTOR.

findings.title: Weapon skins unlock toasts but are never applied to any weapon visual
findings.description: _grantSkin stores PROGRESS._skin_<id> and shows a 'SKIN UNLOCKED' toast, driven from the saveProgress wrapper (30751-30763). But nothing ever reads WEAPON_SKINS or _skin_* to change a weapon's material/appearance (grep across all src finds no equip/apply path; only a telemetry count at 29812). The player is promised cosmetic unlocks that never visibly appear — a half-wired feature.
findings.evidence: 30745 `const s=WEAPON_SKINS[id]; if(s)attachToast('... SKIN UNLOCKED ...');` and grep for WEAPON_SKINS/_skin_ shows only grant + telemetry, no render-time application.
findings.fix: Either implement skin application (read an equipped/highest-tier _skin_* and tint the viewmodel material in the weapon build/switchWeapon path) for a real visible reward, or remove the 'SKIN UNLOCKED' toast so the game doesn't promise something it never shows. The former is the AAA win.
findings.risk: Low for removing the toast. Implementing application is medium (must not touch the disabled GLB paths or add material.skinning).

findings.title: SHAKE_PROFILES + shake(profile) helper is never called; all shake remains scattered ad-hoc
findings.description: A clean named-profile shake system (SHAKE_PROFILES with shoot/bigHit/explosion/takedown/land/etc and a shake(profile) helper writing PP.shakeX/Y and PP.shakeDecay) is defined but never called (grep: only def at 30800 and PP write inside it). Every shake in the game instead pokes PP.shakeX/PP.shakeY inline (dozens of sites 11350..33575), and PP.shakeDecay stays at its init value 11 forever (only set inside the never-called shake()). The intended per-event decay tuning never takes effect.
findings.evidence: 30800 `function shake(profile){ ...PP.shakeX+=...;PP.shakeY-=...;PP.shakeDecay=p.decay; }` no caller; PP.shakeDecay read only at 44524-44525, written only inside shake() — so decay is permanently the init 11.
findings.fix: Wire shake('explosion'|'bigHit'|'takedown'|'land'|'vault') into the corresponding events (grenade/explosion, heavy hit, takedown, landing, vault) to get distinct, AAA-feeling impact decay, OR delete SHAKE_PROFILES+shake if you keep the inline model. Cheap visible upgrade: route the big events (explosion/bigHit/land) through shake() for punchier, faster-settling camera kicks.
findings.risk: Low. Adding calls only adds shake on top of existing; setting PP.shakeDecay per event changes settle speed — verify it feels right and probes still green.

findings.title: Extended SFX library and per-type enemy hit particles defined but unused
findings.description: sfxRicochet, sfxNearMiss, sfxDistantShot, sfxCasingClatter, sfxBodyFall, and the per-enemy-type _enhancedHitParticle (heavy spark burst / drone cyan arc) are fully implemented but never called (only sfxKnifeWhoosh from this block is used, at 14300/19872). sfxImpactFor (31369) routes to sfxRicochet/sfxBodyFall but sfxImpactFor itself is never called either. These are ready-made, low-cost audio/visual juice computed and discarded.
findings.evidence: grep shows no callers for sfxRicochet/sfxNearMiss/sfxDistantShot/sfxCasingClatter/sfxBodyFall/sfxImpactFor/_enhancedHitParticle; _enhancedHitParticle 31375 builds AdditiveBlending sparks into G.trails as isParticle (a live system).
findings.fix: Wire _enhancedHitParticle(hitPoint, enemy.type) into the central enemy-hit handler (near the bullet-hit/blood-spray site) for armored spark bursts on heavy/riot/shielded and cyan arcs on drones. Wire sfxCasingClatter to the eject point on fire, sfxNearMiss when a bullet passes close to the camera, sfxBodyFall on enemy death/ragdoll. Each is a cheap, immediately-visible/audible AAA upgrade.
findings.risk: Low-medium. _enhancedHitParticle pushes into G.trails which already self-disposes via timer; ensure the spawn rate is gated (it spawns 5-8 meshes per hit). Audit that trails cleanup disposes geometry/material (verify isParticle path).

findings.title: Radial 'slow time while picking' is saved but never applied or restored
findings.description: openRadial comments 'Slow time slightly while picking' and stores P._radialPrevScale=P.timeScale, but it never lowers P.timeScale, and closeRadial never reads _radialPrevScale back. The effect is computed (saved) then discarded — the radial does not slow time at all.
findings.evidence: 31404 `// Slow time slightly while picking` 31405 `P._radialPrevScale=P.timeScale;` — grep shows _radialPrevScale is never read again; P.timeScale is never set in open/closeRadial.
findings.fix: If desired, set P.timeScale to e.g. 0.35 in openRadial and restore `P.timeScale=P._radialPrevScale||1` in closeRadial. Otherwise delete the dead _radialPrevScale line. (Lower priority than making the radial clickable at all — see radial-menu-unusable-pointerlock.)
findings.risk: Low. Touching timeScale interacts with focus/killcam time systems (26970/27014); restore carefully so it does not stick.

findings.title: _checkLieuIntro, showLieutenantDeath, _maybeBarkOnAlert, getZoneName, showOperatorDetails are defined but never called
findings.description: Several flavor helpers in scope are dead: _checkLieuIntro (30690) is never called (showLieutenantIntro IS, from 31694 inside it, but the gate fn itself never runs); showLieutenantDeath (31707) never called; _maybeBarkOnAlert (31726) never called; getZoneName/ZONE_NAMES (31560) never called; showOperatorDetails (31735) never called. These are not bugs, but they are unwired content (lieutenant death quotes, zone-clear names, operator detail panel) that the player never sees, and they bloat the contradiction surface.
findings.evidence: grep callers: showLieutenantDeath, _maybeBarkOnAlert, getZoneName, showOperatorDetails, _checkLieuIntro all return zero non-definition matches.
findings.fix: Wire the high-value ones: call showLieutenantDeath(G.building) when a lieutenant dies (alongside the existing death flow), call getZoneName on zone clear for a flavor banner, and add a menu button to showOperatorDetails. Delete the rest if not wanted. Each is content the team already wrote but isn't surfaced.
findings.risk: Low. Adding calls surfaces existing content; verify the lieutenant-death hook fires once.

findings.title: Low-HP heartbeat setInterval runs forever and is never cleared
findings.description: A setInterval(...,1100) at 31367 polls every 1.1s for the life of the page and calls sfxHeartbeat when low HP. It is never cleared. This is benign (cheap, self-gated) but is an unmanaged timer that fires regardless of menu/pause/level-transition state, and creates a WebAudio node pair each beat while low.
findings.fix: Acceptable as-is, but prefer driving the heartbeat from the frame loop (it already gates on G.started/!P.dead) or store the id and clearInterval on teardown for cleanliness. Low priority.
findings.risk: Very low. Behavioral no-op if left.

findings.title: Objective ticker HUD is a flat box — cheap polish opportunity
findings.description: The objective ticker (B05/B07/B10) is created as a plain dark box with a thin progress bar. _refreshObjectiveHud (32044) already computes rich feel values (urgency/holding/cadence/anticipation) and even applies a subtle translateY + boxShadow, but the base element has no entrance animation, no icon glow, and the fill bar transition is a flat 0.1s linear. For a story objective this reads unfinished next to the rest of the polished HUD.
findings.evidence: 32098 inline cssText is a static box; fill 32107 `transition:width .10s linear`; the feel-driven styling at 32057-32065 is good but the static base undercuts it.
findings.fix: Add a CSS entrance (slide+fade-in) on creation, an animated accent glow keyed off feel.objectiveCadence (already computed), and an ease on the fill (cubic-bezier). All driven by values already in _refreshObjectiveHud — near-zero risk, immediately visible during the three story buildings.
findings.risk: Very low. Pure CSS/inline-style polish on an existing element.
